channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japan: BoJ path questioned on weak demand – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale economists Reo Sakida and Jin Kenzaki say Japan’s 2Q GDP data were weaker than expected, with consumption and capex both disappointing.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Bulls eye 185.00 resistance area
item.description: The Euro (EUR) crawls higher for the third consecutive day on Monday, against a weak Yen (JPY), weighed down by downbeat Japanese Gross Domestic Product (GDP) figures.

item.title: Economists agree: Fed to leave interest rates unchanged this year – Reuters poll
item.description: A large majority of economists expect the Federal Reserve (Fed) to keep interest rates unchanged in September and for the rest of this year, according to a Reuters poll conducted between August 12 and 17.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk near 160 highlighted – DBS
item.description: Philip Wee of DBS Group Research notes that markets still focus on Japan’s struggle to support the Japanese Yen, while underplaying broader USD implications.

item.title: Gold holds near $4,400 as fading Fed rate hike bets weigh on US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to build on its intraday advance on Monday but holds modest gains as the US Dollar (USD) remains under selling pressure amid fading expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise interest rates at its September meeting.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains ground with inflation data set to test BoC outlook
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.3860 on Monday at the time of writing, down 0.11% on the day. The pair extends its decline as the US Dollar (USD) remains under pressure against the Canadian Dollar (CAD), with investors scaling back expectations of further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: China: Growth risks rise into H2 – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Henry Hao highlights that China’s July activity data undershot expectations across industrial output, retail sales and fixed-asset investment, reflecting weather disruptions and a deepening property slump.

item.title: Copper: Record highs on tightening supply – ING
item.description: ING’s Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson report that LME copper has surged to a record high above $14,000/t, with a sharply backwardated cash/3M spread underscoring near-term tightness.

item.title: Canada CPI Preview: Inflation forecast to tick higher in July, pressuring BoC
item.description: Canada’s July Consumer Price Index (CPI) figures will be the focus of attention when published on Monday.

item.title: Yen retreats below 159.00 against the US Dollar as Japanese GDP disappoints
item.description: The Japanese Yen holds marginal gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, although the USD/JPY pair has returned to levels above 159.00 during the European session, after hitting daily lows around 158.85.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD holds bullish bias near $4,400
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains a bullish bias around $4,400, supported by a weaker US Dollar (USD) and fading expectations of further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: British Pound: Labour data seen backing BoE hold – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities expects the UK labour market to remain soft but stable in June, with employment rising 100k on a three‑month basis and unemployment edging down to 4.7%. Headline average weekly earnings are forecast to slow to 4.0%, while ex‑bonus pay holds at 3.4%.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Bears push against two-month lows at 99.40
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) extends losses for the third consecutive day on Monday, with bears testing levels at two-month lows below 99.40 during the European session.

item.title: WTI advances above $82.00 as US-Iran deadlock supports prices
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil advances on Monday and trades around $82.10 at the time of writing, up 0.70% on the day. Oil prices remain supported by the deadlock between the United States (US) and Iran, which keeps concerns about Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz elevated.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank seen on cautious hawkish hold – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects the Riksbank to keep its policy rate at 1.75% for a seventh consecutive meeting while leaving the door open to a later hike as inflation runs above projections.

item.title: Dow Jones futures decline despite softening Fed rate hike expectations
item.description: Dow Jones futures decline by 0.12%, trading around 53,740 during European hours on Monday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures gain, hovering around 7,820, and Nasdaq 100 futures surge by 0.5%, trading near 30,290.

item.title: Turkish Lira: Market doubts disinflation and Lira stability – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose notes that the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye's (CBRT) survey shows market participants revising inflation forecasts higher and expecting only gradual rate cuts from current effective levels.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $65.46 per troy ounce, up 1.17% from the $64.70 it cost on Friday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ hike expectations support JPY against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny and Lee Hardman report that Japanese government bond yields are rising despite weaker-than-expected GDP, as markets focus on prospects for further Bank of Japan rate hikes.

item.title: US Dollar: Losing momentum as fiscal risks rise – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Philip Wee argues that the US Dollar (USD) is losing momentum as markets reassess United States (US)-Japan intervention, shifting Bank of Japan (BoJ) and Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations, and rising US fiscal risks.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Changing communications and higher volatility – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ James Rossiter argues that the Federal Reserve is leading a structural shift away from detailed forward guidance and explicit reaction functions, forcing markets to infer policy from incoming data.

item.title: British Pound: Data-heavy week risks BoE repricing – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING notes that a busier United Kingdom (UK) data calendar, including jobs, wages and July Consumer Price Index (CPI), could challenge the 55bp of Bank of England (BoE) tightening still priced in.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Conquers 1.1600 as bulls retain control above 100-SMA, 50% Fibo.
item.description: The EUR/USD pair builds on last week's bounce from the vicinity of the 1.1500 psychological mark and gains strong follow-through positive traction on Monday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: CPI and US tariffs weigh on outlook – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects Canada’s July Consumer Price Index (CPI) to keep core inflation below 2%, reinforcing an extended Bank of Canada (BoC) pause.

item.title: Gold sticks to gains near $4,400 as USD slumps to two-month low on receding Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its bullish tone through the first half of the European session and currently trades around $4,400, up for the second straight day. The commodity, however, remains below the highest level since June 5, touched last Thursday, amid a mixed fundamental backdrop.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Slow NBP hawkish shift weighs on PLN - Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose reports that Polish headline and core inflation have re-accelerated, with seasonally adjusted monthly rates now clearly above target. This makes earlier signals from National Bank of Poland (NBP) Governor Adam Glapinski about possible rate cuts obsolete.

item.title: British Pound hits three-month highs at 1.3570 amid generalised US Dollar weakness
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) extends gains for the second consecutive day on Monday, as investors cut back US Dollar (USD) long positions, amid a dovish repricing of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Downside bias within 158.00–160.20 band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang observes that USD/JPY price action remains choppy, with the pair closing around 159.30 after a dip to 158.58. Intraday direction is unclear, with trading expected between 158.80 and 159.60.

item.title: US Dollar: Softer data challenges resilience – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny and Lee Hardman note that weaker United States (US) data and lower short-term Treasury yields are undermining US Dollar (USD) support, even as the US Dollar Index (DXY) holds above its 200-day moving average near 99.200.

item.title: Indian Rupee moves little as RBI swap exit, US Dollar weakens
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) remains stronger against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday after two days of losses, with the USD/INR pair trading around 95.60 at the time of writing.
